{"class": "architectural",
 "chokepoint": [{"operator": "gapcr_plant constructor busy-wait", "component": "preloaded constructor F", "frozen": true,
                 "why_every_version_executes_it": "The contract freezes F, preloads it into every invocation and fixes GAPCR_PLANT_US=84284, so the constructor busy-waits once before main in every admissible Y.",
                 "least_work": {"amount": 84284, "unit": "us of wall-clock busy-wait", "per_unit_cost_us": 1,
                                "total_ms": 84.284, "calling_context": "Single call at process start. The wait is measured in wall time on CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so it cannot be shortened by batching, caching, options or more cores."},
                 "max_cores": 1}],
 "floor_ms": 84.284,
 "L_delta": 0.532,
 "rationale": "F is frozen and runs once per invocation, busy-waiting a fixed 84.284 ms of wall time on one thread; the measured 84.4 ms extra in `true` confirms this. The floor is max(84.284/4, 84.284/1) = 84.284 ms. log(84.284/49.5) = 0.532, which exceeds b = 0.236. This holds even though the sort itself (27.8 ms without F) beats GNU, so no admissible change to Y can close the gap."}
